conclusions: The minimum viable control is an actor-driven reconciliation loop joining partner identity, current 287(g) status, policy version, active Flock edges, and query activity.
The system should fail closed on stale or ambiguous status and require explicit human recertification.
counterarguments: Automated status feeds may lag or contain identity-matching errors; human review remains necessary.
findings: Eligibility depends on external facts that can change after an agency is approved.
Manual review and a free-text search reason do not create a durable policy boundary.
Public transparency without immutable edge history cannot prove when access was enabled or removed.
limitations: No evidence that Flock currently exposes all required edge/admin events through a public API.
data.method: Timeline reconstruction, claim contradiction analysis, and control-plane observability review.
data.question: What control architecture would prevent a repeat of the 287(g) sharing lag?
recommendations: Ingest authoritative 287(g) rosters with observed timestamps.
Diff against active sharing edges hourly or daily.
Disable prohibited/unknown edges and emit immutable alerts.
Publish signed snapshots and reasoned exceptions.
